text:
maya: incident-bot fired 6:42 — paging for high log error rate on inference-service (v2). lots of 5xx traces, paging everyone. this is noisy, but customers might be impacted. looking now.

incident-bot: Incident created: INC-2026-0421-789 — high rate of inference 5xx. Pager sent to eng-sre rotation.

oncall-bot: @eng-oncall paging maya as primary for rotation. escalation to jon at +5m if no ack.

maya: acked. quick check: dashboards show error rate spike starting ~6:36, correlates with a canary deploy to region-us-west-2.

jon: on it — are these timeouts or explicit 5xx?

maya: logs show mostly `ModelInvocationError: kv-cache-mismatch` and a handful of `502 upstream` during same window. attaching quick grep.

sam: could be a model artifact from the new quantization kernel. the canary used a different kernel selector.

ali: @sam any chance we can flip canary off for the rolling deploy and route traffic back to v1? need live mitigation.

sam: yes — I'm pushing an immediate rollback to canary in us-west-2. command: `kubectl patch svc inference-svc -p '{"spec": {"selector": {"model": "v1"}}}'` — done, watch traffic shift.

maya: traffic shifted ~6:48, error rate dropping in dashboards. still seeing repeated log signature that kept paging: `kv-cache-mismatch: key len 0` in many pods.

jon: put a short suppression on the alert while we validate. set a 30m silence for the rule to avoid repeated pages. we still want to capture if it's real customer impact.

maya: applied suppression window via incident bot: `!suppress alert.log.high-error-rate 00:30 --reason "active mitigation rollback"`

incident-bot: Suppression applied by jon for 30m. alerts will still be recorded but not paged.

tess: quick customer check — no incoming support tickets yet, but prod telemetry shows elevated tail latency for a small subset (0.8% of requests). let's keep eyes on SLO error budget.

ali: post-mortem actions (initial): 1) refine log-based alert query to exclude known benign kv-cache mismatch pattern when below a threshold, 2) create a specific signature for kv-cache-mismatch with high severity if accompanied by 502s, 3) add a dashboard panel to show canary vs baseline kernel selector.

jon: agree. current alert is too broad: it triggers on any >50 error/min in the log stream. that was fine before canaries, now it's noisy. propose change: require `count_distinct(pod)` > 3 or include `status:502` in query to escalate.

maya: draft of tightened LogQL (Datadog/Logsearch style):
```
source:inference-service AND level:error AND NOT message:/kv-cache-mismatch: key len 0/ AND (http_status:[500 TO 599] OR error_count:>50)
```
this excludes the known KV noise unless there are real 5xxs or sustained volume.

sam: alternative: keep the kv-cache-mismatch in logs but add a new signature rule that only pages when `kv-cache-mismatch` AND `http_status:502` appear together within 1 minute window. we can do that with a joint query.

ali: also recommend we implement a regex filter at ingestion for the most frequent benign stacktrace fragment to reduce log volume. regex: `kv-cache-mismatch: key len \d+` -> keep as INFO for now. need to coordinate with logging pipeline owners.

tess: can we add a temporary dashboard tile showing per-kernel error rates? that'll help catch future regressions fast. cc: @eng-platform for quick dashboard build.

jon: created a ticket: INF-4592 — "Alert tuning + kv-cache signature" assigned to sam, priority P1 for this week. includes tasks: update alert query, add signature, add dashboard, add ingestion filter PR.

maya: I've posted a short incident note in #postmortems with timeline. low customer impact, mitigation via rollback completed.

sam: PR for alert query change (draft):
```
- query: count_over_time({service:inference, level:error}[1m]) > 50
+ query: count_over_time({service:inference, level:error, !message:"kv-cache-mismatch"}[1m]) > 50 OR (count_over_time({service:inference, http_status:502}[1m]) > 5 && count_distinct(pod) > 2)
```
open for review.

ali: for the ingestion filter I'll open a branch in logs-ingest with the regex and a toggle flag. we should keep it reversible.

tess: can we add a runbook snippet for "rollback canary" under the incident doc? that helped today. make it first-class.

maya: noted. adding runbook entry and tagging eng-oncall.

jon: follow-up items before close: 1) merge alert query PR, 2) merge ingestion-filter toggle PR, 3) add dashboard panel + template variables, 4) update paging policy doc to require distinct-pod or 502 gating for this alert.

maya: thanks everyone. once PRs are merged we'll lift suppression and monitor for 1h.

incident-bot: Incident INC-2026-0421-789 status changed to Monitoring.

oncall-bot: Hand-off to next on-call in 40m: jon -> ali.

jon: handing off to ali. leaving notes in the incident doc.

ali: taking over. will shepherd the PRs and verify dashboard.

maya: last note — recommend adding an automatic canary-rollback policy when X% 5xx detected within Y minutes to avoid manual steps next time. filing infra proposal.

sam: filed infra proposal INF-4596 for auto-rollback heuristics.

maya: closing thread here; will update when postmortem is ready. :white_check_mark:
